question: The original Constitution of 1950 envisaged a Supreme Court with a Chief Justice and ________ puisne Judges - leaving it to Parliament to increase this number.
solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original Constitution of 1950 envisaged a Supreme Court with a Chief Justice and **7** puisne Judges.
 
• It was left to Parliament to increase this number as required.
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal as established by the Constitution.
 
• It has extensive powers in the form of original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions.
 
• The number of judges in the Supreme Court has been increased from time to time to handle the increasing number of cases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on January 28, 1950.
 
• It succeeded the Federal Court of India, which had been established under the Government of India Act 1935.
 
• The Supreme Court initially sat in the Chamber of Princes in the Parliament House, before moving to its present building.
 
• The Constitution of India provides for the independence of the judiciary, ensuring that judges are free from any influence from the executive or legislative branches of government.
 
• The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President of India and serves until the age of 65.
 
• The Supreme Court has the power of judicial review to ensure the constitutionality of laws.
 
• As of now, the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court is 34 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.
